events.title: BlackHat MEA CTF Final 2026
events.description: Black Hat MEA Capture The Flag (CTF) 2026 ? The Black Hat MEA Capture The Flag (CTF) is the largest cybersecurity competition in the region and officially the largest Capture The Flag competition in the world, recognized with a Guinness World Record. Organized by the Saudi Federation for Cybersecurity, Programming and Drones (SAFCSP) in collaboration with Black Hat MEA, the competition brings together thousands of cybersecurity professionals, researchers, students, and enthusiasts from around the globe. Powered by the FlagYard platform, the competition follows a Jeopardy-style format, where teams of 3–5 players compete across a range of cybersecurity challenges, including Web Exploitation, PWN, Digital Forensics, Reverse Engineering, Cryptography, and AI Hacking. Competition Timeline Registration: June 3 – August 29, 2026 Online Qualifiers: August 29, 2026 | 10:00 AM KSA (GMT+3) | Online Thousands of participants will compete globally in teams of 3–5 members, with the top 150 teams qualifying for the final stage. On-site Finals The top 150 teams will be invited to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia for a 3-day final competition during Black Hat MEA, taking place from December 1–3, 2026. Register Now: https://flagyard.com/events/3468f495-a92c-498b-90c2-994dfb99ea0b Support: blackhatctf@safcsp.org.sa

events.title: Leo's 20th Birthday Bash
events.description: Hey! You there! Do you like programming? Do you like puzzles? Do you like... money? Leo's 20th Birthday Bash is a 24-hour online team contest that's competitive-programming-ish, CTF-ish, math-olympiad-ish, and puzzle-hunt-ish, all wrapped into one. The contest runs on DMOJ, an online judge for competitive programming, and each team shares one DMOJ account to submit from. Teams can have 1 to 10 members (6 to 8 recommended). Some problems are CTF-ish, but DMOJ itself is not part of the contest, so please do not attack, probe, or abuse it. The people at DMOJ are hosting this for free >.< This contest has no sponsors, so all the prize money is from yours truly ;) Make sure you've read all the rules (see the contest page). In particular, interactive generative AI is not allowed, because it is stinky. See you there!

events.title: OTERIA Cyber Cup #4
events.description: # OTERIA Cyber ​​Cup #4 Rejoignez-nous le 12 décembre 2026 pour la quatrième édition de l'OTERIA Cyber ​​Cup, une compétition de type « Capture The Flag » (CTF) destinée aux étudiants, organisée par l'OTERIA Cyber ​​School à Gennevilliers, en France. events.title: Cyber Ninja CTF 2026 - BLACKOUT
events.description: RÉSERVÉ UNIQUEMENT AUX LYCÉENS # Cyber Ninja CTF 2026 – BLACKOUT Gardez Paris allumé ! Le Cyber Ninja CTF revient pour sa 3e édition avec BLACKOUT, une compétition nationale de cybersécurité organisée par OTERIA Cyber School et destinée aux lycéens de toute la France. Cette année, un mystérieux hacker surnommé « Lights-Out » menace les infrastructures critiques de Paris : métro, électricité, réseaux de communication et distribution d'eau. Votre mission : résoudre des challenges de cybersécurité, récupérer des flags, découvrir des indices cachés et arrêter Lights-Out avant que Paris ne soit plongé dans le noir. ## Dates et déroulement Qualifications en ligne - Début : samedi 19 décembre 2026 à 10h (heure de Paris) - Fin : dimanche 20 décembre 2026 à 10h (heure de Paris) - Durée : 24 heures - Format : Jeopardy - Participation : individuelle et gratuite Finale en présentiel - Date : samedi 16 janvier 2027 - Lieu : campus OTERIA, région parisienne - Participants : les 80 meilleurs des qualifications éligibles - Invité spécial : V2F, youtubeur spécialisé en cybersécurité ## Les challenges Une cinquantaine de flags répartis dans 9 catégories : - Web : exploitation de vulnérabilités Web - PWN : exploitation de programmes binaires - Reverse Engineering : rétro-ingénierie - Crypto : cryptographie - OSINT : recherche en sources ouvertes - DFIR : investigation numérique et réponse aux incidents - Hardware : sécurité matérielle - Programming : programmation - Misc : challenges divers Trois niveaux de difficulté sont proposés : débutant, intermédiaire et confirmé. Aucune expérience préalable en cybersécurité n'est nécessaire pour participer. ## Un scénario immersif : BLACKOUT Pendant les qualifications, certains flags permettront de débloquer des éléments du dossier « Lights-Out » : messages interceptés, photographies, notes manuscrites et indices cachés. Ces informations pourront aider les participants à progresser dans les challenges et à découvrir les prochaines cibles du hac

events.title: THE FINAL EXPLOIT CTF 2026—QUALIFIERS
events.description: THE FINAL EXPLOIT CTF 2026 — QUALIFIERS ONE LAST FLAG. ONE FINAL EXPLOIT. The year is coming to an end, but there's one last challenge waiting. Organized by 0xV01D, THE FINAL EXPLOIT CTF 2026 is a 48-hour international online Jeopardy-style competition, open to CTF teams worldwide. Compete against teams from around the world, solve challenging cybersecurity problems, demonstrate your real-world skills, and earn your place in THE FINAL EXPLOIT CTF 2026 — GRAND FINAL. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ EVENT DETAILS Dates: December 29–31, 2026 Start: December 29 at 12:00 UTC End: December 31 at 12:00 UTC Duration: 48 hours Format: Online | Jeopardy-style Participation: Team-based | Worldwide Organizer: 0xV01D Prizes: To be announced ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ CHALLENGE CATEGORIES • Web Exploitation • Binary Exploitation (Pwn) • Reverse Engineering • Cryptography • OSINT • Digital Forensics & Incident Response (DFIR) • Malware Analysis • Mobile Security • AI Security • Blockchain Security • Miscellaneous BEYOND TRADITIONAL CTF CHALLENGES This competition goes beyond conventional CTF puzzles. Participants will face realistic, industry-inspired cybersecurity scenarios designed to test practical skills used by security professionals in real-world environments. Expect hands-on challenges involving: • Security Operations Center (SOC) investigations and threat detection • Real-world penetration testing methodologies and exploitation scenarios • Digital forensics and incident response investigations • Analysis of authentic or realistically simulated security logs, network traffic, and system artifacts • Threat hunting, attack reconstruction, and incident analysis • Practical security challenges inspired by real operational environments These challenges are designed to bridge the gap between CTF competitions and the cybersecurity industry, encouraging participants to develop job-relevant skills in offensive and defensive security. NOT JUST FLAGS. REAL SKILLS. REAL-WORLD SECURITY. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
